Scaffold a minimal package on disk for trying out cranlint checks

Source: R/example-pkg.R
cl_example_pkg.Rd

Writes a valid, minimal package (a DESCRIPTION file, and optionally R/ and man/ files) to a new temporary directory. This exists to support the runnable @examples on cl_check_*()/lint_cran(), and to make it easy to try cranlint out interactively, without needing a real package on disk – it is not part of the actual linting logic.

Usage

cl_example_pkg(description = character(), r_files = list(), man_files = list())

Arguments

description

A named character vector of DESCRIPTION fields to add or override on top of a minimal default (Package, Title, Version, Authors@R, Description, License).

r_files

A named list mapping a filename (e.g. "foo.R") to a character vector of lines, written under R/.

man_files

A named list mapping a filename (e.g. "foo.Rd") to a character vector of lines, written under man/.

Value

The path to the scaffolded package (a tempdir). Callers should unlink(path, recursive = TRUE) once done with it.

Examples

pkg_dir <- cl_example_pkg(
  description = c(Description = "Does a thing."),
  r_files = list(simulate.R = c(
    "simulate <- function() {",
    "  set.seed(42)",
    "  rnorm(1)",
    "}"
  ))
)
lint_cran(pkg_dir)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   check              file          line severity   message      policy_reference
#>   <chr>              <chr>        <int> <ord>      <chr>        <chr>           
#> 1 description_length DESCRIPTION     NA should_fix The Descrip… https://contrib…
#> 2 hardcoded_seed     R/simulate.R     2 should_fix set.seed() … https://contrib…
unlink(pkg_dir, recursive = TRUE)
